name: @oscharko-dev/keiko-ui
description: Keiko Wave 1 local UI (static export). Build-time-only; served by the Node BFF in keiko-server.

scripts.typecheck:native: npm --prefix ../.. run check:typescript-toolchain && node ../../node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --incremental false

_browserslistRationale: Corrected from chrome/edge>=79, firefox>=72, safari>=13.1, which the shipped UI code has not
satisfied for a long time: Array.prototype.at(-n) appears 35 times across 22 production files
Object.hasOwn 7 times across 6 (Firefox 92), and lib/api.ts uses AbortSignal.timeout (Firefox
100, Safari 16) — every one beyond the old floor, so the declaration promised engines on which
the app cannot start. Counts are occurrences and files stated separately on purpose: the
gate's own messages report FILES, and conflating the two produced three wrong numbers here.
AbortSignal.any (Chrome 116, Firefox 124, Safari 17.4) sits above even these floors and is
feature-detected with a fallback in lib/api.ts rather than raising them further.
These floors correspond to the Baseline 'widely available' set and cover every JS API the UI
calls; CSS is NOT yet scanned by the gate, and :has() (Firefox 121) is used in module CSS.
Enterprise Windows fleets run evergreen Edge/Chrome, so this is not a reachability change for
them; it makes the declaration true. check:browser-baseline enforces it against the source.
